title: Hira: "Read!"
hook: A man alone in a mountain cave is told to read. He answers that he can't.

screens.text: **A cave on a mountain. A voice tells him to read.** He answers that he can't. You met this moment on Day 15. This is the rest of that night, and the woman who held him through it.
**Alone with Allah.** In the years before, he had come to love being alone. He would spend nights worshipping in a cave called Hira, outside Makkah, then return to Khadijah for more food [Bukhari 3].
bubbles: He was forty, about 610 CE [Bukhari 3902; Yaqeen]. It was a Monday [Muslim 1162], in **Ramadan** according to most scholars [Q 2:185; Qalam ep. 28].

screens.text: **Shaking, he went home.** His heart pounding, he asked Khadijah to cover him. She wrapped him up, listened, and reassured him: Allah would never disgrace a man who kept family ties, helped the weak and honoured guests [Bukhari 3].
bubbles: She didn't panic or argue. She reminded him of who he already was.

screens.text: From the cave to the pause.

events.title: In the cave
events.text: The angel tells him to read. The first verses of the Qur'an come down [Bukhari 3; Q 96:1–5].

events.title: Home to Khadijah
events.text: She covers him and reminds him of his good character [Bukhari 3].

events.title: To Waraqah
events.text: Her elderly Christian cousin recognises the angel as the one sent to Musa [Bukhari 3].

events.title: Silence
events.text: Waraqah dies, and revelation pauses for a while [Bukhari 3].

screens.text: **An old Christian scholar.** Khadijah took him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal, an elderly, blind Christian who knew the scripture. Waraqah said it was the same angel Allah had sent to **Musa** (Moses) [Bukhari 3].
bubbles: Waraqah also warned that his own people would drive him out, and said he'd stand by him if he lived to see that day [Bukhari 3].

screens.prompt: When he came home frightened, how did Khadijah reassure him?

options.text: She reminded him of the good he did for family, the weak and guests
options.feedback: Right. She pointed to his character: Allah would never disgrace a man like that [Bukhari 3].

options.text: She told him it was only a bad dream
options.feedback: Not quite. She took it seriously, comforted him, and then found someone who could help.

options.text: She told him to keep it a secret from everyone
options.feedback: Not quite. She took him straight to Waraqah, who knew the earlier scriptures.

screens.text: **The person beside you.** At the most frightening moment of the Prophet's ﷺ life, his wife listened, reminded him of his good, and found him help. When you're shaken, you need someone like that. And you can be that person for someone else.

screens.situation: Hannah has been Muslim a month. Late one night her friend Dre calls, shaken: he's just lost his job and is sure his life is falling apart.

options.text: Listen first, remind him of the good he does, and help him find someone who can help
options.feedback: Yes. That's what Khadijah did: listen, remind, then find help. Calm presence is worth more than a speech.

options.text: Tell him to pray about it and get off the phone
options.feedback: Not quite. Prayer helps, but he needs someone to listen first. Khadijah heard the whole story.

options.text: Give him a long lecture on what he should have done
options.feedback: Not quite. In a scary moment, people need comfort before advice.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- He came to love solitude and spent nights worshipping in the cave of Hira, returning to Khadijah for provisions [Bukhari 3].
- The angel told him to read; he said he could not; the first revelation was the opening of Surah al-'Alaq [Bukhari 3; Q 96:1–5]. Day 15 already teaches this; build on it.
- He was forty [Bukhari 3902], about 610 CE [Yaqeen; Dar al-Ifta Egypt, seerah part 4]. It was a Monday [Muslim 1162], in Ramadan according to most scholars [Qalam ep. 28; Q 2:185]. The day of the month is disputed (14th, 17th, 21st, 27th are all reported).
- He came home with his heart pounding and asked to be covered; Khadijah reassured him that Allah would never disgrace a man who kept family ties, helped the weak and honoured guests [Bukhari 3].
- She took him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal, an elderly, blind Christian who wrote from the Gospel in Hebrew; Waraqah said it was the same angel sent to Musa, warned that his people would drive him out, and said he would support him if he lived. A few days later Waraqah died and revelation paused [Bukhari 3].

**Likely questions**
- *"Why did he say he couldn't read?"* He couldn't read or write; the hadith tells it plainly [Bukhari 3]. The message didn't come from his own study.
- *"Was the angel rough with him?"* The hadith says the angel held him tightly three times before the verses came [Bukhari 3]. Tell it calmly, without dramatising, and don't explain why beyond the text.
- *"Was Waraqah a Muslim?"* Say what the hadith says: he recognised the angel and said he would support him, then died a few days later. Don't speculate about his fate.
- *"Which night of Ramadan?"* Most scholars say Ramadan; the exact night is disputed. Laylat al-Qadr questions can go to the ramadan modules.
- *"How do I support someone who's frightened?"* Listen first, remind them of their good, then help them find the right person (mentor, counsellor, imam). If anyone is in danger, follow the safety rule.

**Escalate:** nothing specific to this lesson; any crisis a convert describes follows the safety rule.

**Don't**
- Don't repeat Day 15's teaching at length; point back to it.
- Don't describe the angel's appearance, and don't picture the Prophet ﷺ, Jibril or Khadijah.
- Don't speak negatively of Christianity; Waraqah was a Christian who believed him (see Day 27).
